title: MZ Is it worth starting a new project in MZ or should I wait for the next RPG maker version?

posts.author: Wildschwein
posts.body:
Is it worth starting a long-term project in RPG Maker MZ, or should I wait for the next RPG Maker version to release first?
I fear that I could start my project in MZ, and then the next RPG Maker releases with more features, and I will have to start all over again.
I think I would work on my game for at least a few months.
Plz help!

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body: Everyone here knows as much as you, we don't even know whether it's a "new" maker or just an MV3D integration into MZ.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Wildschwein said:
next RPG Maker releases with more features, and I will have to start all over again.
Click to expand...
That's why you know what features your game will need before you start.
Does MZ and its plugins do what you want? Use it. They've only just teased an alleged new version with 2dhd. Who knows when that's gonna be out (assuming it is a new Maker). There will always be some new engine somewhere. Don't get trapped in waiting for "the right one".

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body: MZ must be nearly stable. There are some advantages in using a stable engine over something that every second new version causes existing plugins not to work.

posts.author: JGreene
posts.body:
The new engine appears to be Octopath style, which is cool. But, plugins similar to that already exist, like
MV3D
and
Chrono Engine
.
However, it doesn't mean that people don't still enjoy regular 2D games. Definitely don't wait to make the game you've envisioned. You can always improve it over time as you think of new ideas. But, you can't improve something that isn't there.

posts.author: satilte
posts.body:
If you're looking to make use of the preview's 2.5D look, there are other engines that achieve the aesthetic (RPG Developer Bakin, RPG Paper Maker). MV/MZ also have 2.5D/3D plugins, but they take a bit of know-how and time to set up. If you're making a short RPG for a few months, I don't see how a change in RPGM engines could affect development unless the new engine release* (we still don't know if it is an engine) has radical changes to systems and overhauls RPG Maker staples; I'd say just go for it and make use of the resources available here.
I'm also excited for a potentially new engine, though I doubt it'll be more than a few engine updates and modern amenities, plus the 3D style they have going on in the preview.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: As stated above, if you want to make a 2.5D/Octopath-style RPG game there are several engines (Bakin, RPG Paper Maker, RPG Architect) available now with 80-90 percent positive ratings. We don't know anything else about the new engine so don't know if there is anything else worth waiting for.
